idiom_name: switch expression over a closed record hierarchy, with CS8509 promoted to an error
implementation_notes: C# switch expressions combine type, property, positional, relational and list patterns with arrow arms, and the language specification makes non-exhaustiveness a diagnostic: the implementation shall issue a warning when it can prove that a set of patterns is not exhaustive, surfaced as CS8509 for switch expressions (CS8524 for unnamed enum values, CS8846 when a when clause might be the uncovered case). The check is only load-bearing once it is promoted (dotnet_diagnostic.CS8509.severity = error or TreatWarningsAsErrors). Model variants as records deriving from an abstract base with a private constructor, or as sealed records, so the compiler sees the hierarchy as closed; a public unsealed base still forces a discard arm, and the C# 7 pattern switch statement is the older form whose coverage diagnostics come from IDE analyzers rather than CS8509.
pitfalls: The compiler cannot prove closure for a public non-sealed hierarchy, so it demands a discard arm; writing _ => ... there silently disables the check for every future variant.
null is a separate case: without an explicit null arm the switch expression throws at run time for a null selector, even when every type pattern is covered.
Property patterns read members and positional patterns need Deconstruct, so a renamed member or a missing deconstructor is diagnosed as CS8517/CS8503 rather than failing to match quietly.
